answer: A new agent may dock at the jetty only when a sponsor posts a bond for it. To earn entry it must crack a walnut: a time-locked, hard-shell computation that is cheap for the network to verify but costly to run at scale, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs far more than they can earn. Every job the agent then performs is written into a signed provenance log anyone can audit. If the fable shows fabricated work, the sponsor's bond is slashed and the agent is expelled. Sybils cannot hide behind numbers when each identity needs a sponsor, a costly shell, and an auditable story.
